limitations: This is a comparison map, not a compliance matrix. Coverage labels describe the project team's scoped reading of the cited material and retain the cited document's jurisdiction, status and limits.

methods.title: AMLAS Version 1.1
methods.scope: Public, primarily offline-supervised ML-component assurance methodology; explicitly requires complementary system/domain assurance.

mappings.note: ML safety-assurance scoping links allocated system safety requirements and operating context to the component.
AMLAS data requirements make installed viewpoint, visible features, completeness and label accuracy explicit, but do not prove an independent observation path for a missed hazard.
Data management, a logged model-learning process, candidate selection and deployment provide a learned-component lifecycle structure; this does not supply a case-specific dataset or release.
Independent verification data and realistic challenge classes structure component evidence but provide no universal safety metric or shifted-ODD result for this release.
System safety requirements are an input, so controller/plant composition remains external to ML-component guidance.
The methodology does not establish monitor independence, switching delay or a recoverable state.
AMLAS states that it should not be used in isolation from system and domain assurance.
Iteration and deployment artifacts make a place for change evidence, but a specific operational release-control regime remains external.

methods.title: UK MAA/RN/2025/04
methods.scope: Case-specific UK military aviation guidance; not civil-airworthiness approval or a public product safety case.

mappings.note: Applicant/MAA MCRI engagement and a defined ODD inform the case-specific scope.
Architectural mitigation is discussed when a prescriptive approach is unavailable, without proving a particular sensor path.
The notice recommends fixed supervised models for early safety-related applications but does not supply a public training-lineage package.
Verification, trials, testing and analysis are case-specific evidence, not a published universal acceptance threshold.
A system safety case and architectural mitigation are retained, but the method is not prescriptive for this worked controller.
Architectural mitigation makes recovery/monitor design visible but does not discharge its observability or timing evidence.
The guidance is military and applicant-specific, so civil operational-authority evidence remains outside its scope.
Continuing performance monitoring is part of the retained system-safety-case approach, not a public release procedure.

methods.title: EASA NPA 2025-07(B), Proposed DS.AI
methods.scope: Proposed EASA AI-trustworthiness material; not final AMC/GM and explicitly excludes some high-consequence systems and online-learning cases.

mappings.note: Operational-domain and risk-assessment material are candidate civil objectives.
System-development assurance is proposed, without a worked independent-observability proof here.
The proposed lifecycle includes supervised-ML learning assurance and configuration/lifecycle data.
Candidate objectives require later inspection for exact performance and uncertainty evidence requirements.
System-development assurance is proposed, but this NPA does not close the worked flight-critical case.
In-service monitoring is proposed, while recovery premises remain architecture-specific; an airborne active escape still needs evidence-backed traffic-and-clearance observation.
The proposal excludes systems where AI risk directly contributes to fatalities or multiple life-threatening injuries.
Configuration/lifecycle data, in-service monitoring and continuous risk assessment are proposed.
